seo.description: Ras El Ma (Cap de l’Eau): a quieter Mediterranean beach town east of Nador for swimming and coastal pace.

name: Ras El Ma (Cap de l’Eau)
hero_subtitle: A calmer coastal town and beach east of Nador — sand, fishing boats and open Mediterranean light.

overview.title: Slower coast east of town
overview.p1: Ras El Ma, also known as Cap de l’Eau, is a small coastal town with beaches that feel less urban than Nador’s lagoon front.
overview.p2: Come for sand, swimming and a fishing-town rhythm. It works as a full beach day or a half-day escape when you want open sea rather than lagoon edges.
overview.p3: Services are modest; bring what you need for sun and water.

food.title: Food in Ras El Ma
food.p1: Expect simple coastal cooking — grilled fish, cafés and modest local tables rather than a long fine-dining strip.
food.li1: Fresh fish when fishing boats are active.
food.li2: Cafés for tea and a pause after the beach.
food.li3: Pack snacks if you arrive outside meal hours.
food.li4: A return dinner on the Nador corniche is always an option.
food.li5: Ask locally what was landed the same day.
food.p2: Beach pace and simple plates, not a restaurant destination.

faq.title: Ras El Ma (Cap de l’Eau) FAQ

q1.question: How far from Nador?
q1.answer: East along the coast — plan transfer time into your day.

q2.question: Family friendly?
q2.answer: Often used by families; still respect sea conditions.

q3.question: Compared with Charrana?
q3.answer: Both are calmer beach options; Charrana is more cove-and-cliff, Ras El Ma more small-town coast.

q4.question: Food?
q4.answer: Simple local options; packing a picnic is wise outside peak hours.

q5.question: Best season?
q5.answer: Late spring through early autumn for swimming.
